risks.note: Management states 'margin pressure from imported PVC resin and Chinese competition remains a major concern' even while calling the 2025-2030 market outlook structurally positive, and lists as important industry dynamics that 'India remains heavily dependent on imported PVC resin', 'Chinese oversupply is suppressing prices globally' and 'Domestic players are lobbying for anti-dumping and BIS protections'. It separately warns that 'Volatility in raw material prices due to fluctuation in resin prices may hinder industry expansion over coming years'. This is the sharpest structural risk in the report because the Company is a single-input, single-polymer manufacturer with no disclosed backward integration - management itself notes 'Backward integration is becoming a key competitive advantage' without claiming to have any, so the relief valve it identifies is one it does not hold. Any protection would come from anti-dumping/BIS action the Company does not control.
risks.risk: Imported PVC resin dependence and Chinese oversupply - a structural squeeze on the Company's only input and its selling prices

risks.note: The MD&A states 'The Company is engaged only in single segment of products i.e. PVC products'; BRSR Section A item 16 shows one main activity, Manufacturing, at 100% of turnover; and BRSR item 18 records just one national plant (plus two offices), the Boisar facility in Palghar district, Thane, Maharashtra. Every rupee of standalone revenue therefore depends on one polymer, one process family and one physical site - fire, flood, labour action, a Maharashtra pollution-control order or a resin-supply interruption at Boisar has no fallback. A second, international plant appears in the BRSR location table but is never named, located or described anywhere in the report, so it cannot be relied on as redundancy.
risks.risk: Single-segment, single-domestic-plant concentration - no diversification anywhere in the operating structure

risks.note: BRSR item 19(b) puts exports at 30.45% of total turnover, with more than 300 international distributors across 70 countries and an extensive retail presence in Europe and North America - i.e. roughly a third of standalone revenue sits outside India's jurisdiction and currency. Management links this directly to FY26 damage, commenting in the key-ratio disclosure that 'Surged tariffs and escalating war tension impacted the business of the Company' and that 'Geopolitical tensions and war increased global instability and economic stress' (the associated ratio figures are deliberately not reproduced here). This is a stated, realised risk rather than a hypothetical one, and the Company has no disclosed hedging, alternative-market or tariff-mitigation plan.
risks.risk: Export concentration colliding with tariffs and war - management explicitly attributes damage to it this year

risks.note: Management's own commentary on its key financial ratios flags a material lengthening of debtor days, explained by surged tariffs and escalating war tension, and a decline in interest coverage explained by geopolitical tension and war; it also notes the current ratio rose because of an increase in trade receivables coupled with a decrease in short-term borrowings. Read qualitatively, cash is being absorbed into receivables rather than released, and the improvement in one headline liquidity ratio is partly an artefact of that absorption - a durable watch-item for anyone tracking this company. Numeric ratio values are deliberately not reproduced here.
risks.risk: Receivables and working-capital stretch tied to the export channel

risks.note: The MD&A states that as on March 31, 2026 the Company had 273 employees against 358 in the previous year - a reduction of roughly a quarter of the payroll in a single year - while asserting industrial relations at the factory 'have remained cordial' and offering no explanation for the decline. The BRSR reports 275 permanent employees and 102 permanent workers at the same date, which does not reconcile with the MD&A's 273 figure, and reports permanent-employee turnover of 9.02% in FY26 against 8.15% and 2.16% in the two prior years (a rising trend), with the permanent-workers turnover row left entirely blank. For a business whose only manufacturing know-how sits at one site, a shrinking and increasingly mobile workforce with contradictory reporting is a structural, not cosmetic, concern.
risks.risk: Sharp workforce contraction and inconsistent headcount disclosure

risks.note: The BRSR material-issues table identifies Product Safety and Quality (classified, oddly, as an Opportunity) and states that 'any loose end in the product maintenance or quality may pose it to material risks', with financial implications spelled out as product recalls, damaged consumer quality perception, reputational harm and increased costs from replacements, field service, product fixes and litigation. The MD&A reinforces the regulatory leg: 'stringent regulations related to volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emissions coupled with changing environmental policies could also affect overall business prospects during forecasted timeframe'. PVC flooring sold into healthcare, education and transportation is exactly the category where VOC and indoor-air-quality rules tighten first, and roughly a third of output goes to jurisdictions (Europe, North America) that regulate this most aggressively. NOTE A CLEAR TEMPLATE DEFECT IN THIS ROW: the mitigation text reads 'Our product responsibility extends beyond manufacturing and sales, contributing to cleaner and safer mobility' - 'mobility' is automotive-sector boilerplate that does not describe a PVC flooring and synthetic-leather business, indicating this material-issue row was copied from another company's BRSR.
risks.risk: Product safety, quality and VOC/environmental regulation of PVC products

risks.note: Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a Risk with negative financial implications: 'technology failures or cyberattacks can disrupt operations, leading to downtime and loss of productivity'. Stated mitigations are firewalls, encryption, multi-factor authentication, regular security audits, employee education and adoption of global data protection standards, plus regular assessment for system vulnerabilities, compliance gaps and technological obsolescence. No incidents, breaches or spend are disclosed, and there is no board-level technology committee.

The first material issue in the BRSR table, classified as a Risk: 'Non-compliance of code of conduct and business ethics affects the work environment and profitability of the Company and may also cause financial or reputational impact', with negative financial implications from disruption and reputational damage. The only stated mitigation is regular employee training on the Code of Conduct. This risk sits alongside a related-party disclosure whose AOC-2 paragraph is self-contradictory (it simultaneously suggests material related-party transactions may exist and that no information need be provided) and a BRSR that reports the entire related-party-share block as dashes.
